name: Documentary Label Tableau
description: One extraordinary natural-history subject or Earth-scale event, composed as a calm cinematic tableau with a short model-rendered documentary label that complements the full episode title.
composition_guidance: Build one original, immediately legible natural-history cover around a single extraordinary landscape, organism, fossil, ocean world, human ancestor, map, or Earth-system event. The image should communicate scale and atmosphere before detail.
composition_rules: Use one dominant hero subject or one uninterrupted wide vista; never a collage.
Reserve one clean left-side text zone, usually lower-left but upper-left when the subject requires it. Render the exact generated label there in large bold white uppercase sans-serif lettering.
Keep the label to two or three compact lines within safe margins, with enough local contrast to remain readable at phone size.
Use strong foreground, midground, and background layering with restrained atmosphere. The subject stays readable even when the artwork is generated by a lower-cost image model.
Let the full episode title carry the detailed explanation; the thumbnail label supplies category, scale, time, or one truthful point of curiosity.
required_elements: one dominant natural-history subject, process, or vista
avoid_elements: the full episode title, explanatory paragraphs, diagrams, callouts, or a dense montage
more than two competing focal subjects
small serif captions, low-contrast lettering, misspelled text, placeholder text, or post-render overlays
copied channel marks, broadcaster branding, logos, duration badges, player UI, watermarks, or another creator’s trade dress
glossy plastic CGI, generic disaster spectacle, unsupported scientific certainty, or irrelevant human hosts
headline_guidance: Read the episode title and create the exact in-image label. If the title is a Deep Rest episode ending in “Documentary for Sleep”, use exactly “DOCUMENTARY FOR SLEEP”. Otherwise write a truthful 2–5 word factual label that adds useful contrast to the full title: a time marker, transformed world, decisive process, organism group, or central mystery. Never merely shorten the title, invent a claim, or use empty bait.
visual_style_guidance: Original painterly natural-history documentary tableau with readable organisms, landscapes, fossils, oceans, maps, and Earth processes; soft atmospheric depth, restrained premium editorial texture, teal water, mossy green, dawn amber, or volcanic ochre. The selected project visual art style remains the final rendering authority.
